units.title: Population and Our Future
units.intro: Grammar: talking about the future and conditional sentences type 1 (real/possible) and type 2 (unreal/imaginary).

cards.title: Conditionals type 1 and 2
rule: **Type 1 (real possibility):** *If + present simple, will + base verb.* *If the population **grows** fast, we **will need** more schools.*

**Type 2 (unreal or unlikely now/future):** *If + past simple, would + base verb.* *If I **had** more land, I **would grow** more food.* With be, use **were** for all persons in formal English: *If I **were** you, ...*
The if-clause can come second; then no comma: *We will need more schools if the population grows.*

examples.text: If it rains, we will stay inside.
If it will rain, we will stay inside.
examples.fix: If it rains, we will stay inside.

examples.text: If I were rich, I would build a hospital.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: **1: present → will. 2: past → would.** Never put will/would in the if-part.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Type 1: if + present, will + verb for real future possibilities. Type 2: if + past, would + verb for unreal or unlikely situations (If I were ...). Unless means if not.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The official report on the regional economic development ________ by the committee before the deadline last night.

steps.text: The subject 'The official report' is inanimate and cannot perform the action of submitting.
The time-marker 'last night' indicates the Simple Past tense, requiring the past passive form ($$\text{was/were} + \text{V}_3$$).

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: A massive amount of money ________ currently ________ to fund the construction of the new school library.

steps.text: The subject is 'A massive amount of money' (singular and inanimate), requiring the passive voice.
The time-marker 'currently' indicates an action in progress, requiring the Present Progressive Passive ($$\text{is/are} + \text{being} + \text{V}_3$$).
Students often choose 'is raising' (Option A) because they confuse active and passive progressive forms.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The high school teacher ________ a beautiful traditional gift by the students on her graduation day.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
This is a double-object passive where the Indirect Object 'The high school teacher' is placed in the subject position: $$\text{IO} + \text{be} + \text{V}_3 + \text{DO}$$.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often choose 'gave' (Option A) because they see a person as the subject and assume the active voice. However, the context shows she received the gift, requiring the passive form 'was given' (Option B).

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
እቲ መምህር ባዕሉ ህያብ ኣይሃበን፤ বልኩስ ካብ ተመሃሮ ህያብ ተዋሂብዎ (received)። እዚ ዓይነት መዋቕር ድርብ ተቐባሊ ዘለዎ ግሲ (double-object passive) ኮይኑ፡ 'was given' (Option B - ተዋሂቡ) ቅኑዕ መልሲ ይኸውን። 'gave' እንተይልና እቲ መምህር ባዕሉ ንተመሃሮ ህያብ ሂብዎም ማለት ምኾነ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The national examination papers ________ by next Friday afternoon, according to the official schedule.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The inanimate subject 'examination papers' requires the passive voice. The time-marker 'by next Friday' indicates a future point of completion, requiring the Future Perfect Passive ($$\text{will have been} + \text{V}_3$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often see 'next Friday' and choose active 'will print' (Option A) or active future perfect 'will have printed' (Option D). Because papers cannot print themselves, the passive 'will have been printed' (Option B) is correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'By next Friday' (ክሳብ ዝመጽእ ዓርቢ) ዝብል ሓረግ መጻኢ ፍጹም እዋን (Future Perfect) ከም ዘድልየና የረድኣና። እቲ ዋና ባእታ 'examination papers' (መፈተኒ ወረቐት) ህይወት ኣልቦ ስለ ዝኾነ ድማ እቲ ምሉእ ሓሳብ ኣብ Future Perfect Passive 'will have been printed' (Option B - ተሓቲሙ ክውዳእ እዩ) ክስራዕ ኣለዎ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Unless you beg me, I ___ you the money.
cards.why: **Unless** means 'if not'. The sentence means 'If you don't beg me, I won't give you the money'. This is a Type 1 conditional.

why: Answer C: If we plant more trees, the soil will be protected.

questions.q: Read: "Eritrea's population is young: many people are under 25. If more young people get skills and jobs, the economy will grow faster. If they cannot find work, many may leave the country." What does the writer suggest?
questions.label: 14. Read: "Eritrea's population is young: many people are under 25. If more young people get skills and…

similar.q: Find a type 1 conditional in the passage.
similar.a: "If more young people get skills and jobs, the economy will grow faster."

similar.q: What may happen if young people cannot find work?
similar.a: Many may leave the country.

options.A: The economy will grow without skills.
options.B: Young people should leave the country.
options.C: Jobs and training for young people are important for the economy.

why: Answer C: Jobs and training for young people are important for the economy.
The first sentence says the population is young.
The conditionals show two outcomes: with skills and jobs the economy grows; without work people may leave.
So the writer stresses jobs and training.
questions.tip: Type 1 (real future): If + present, will + verb. Type 2 (unreal present/future): If + past, would + verb.

similar.q: Zero conditional: If you mix blue and yellow, you ____ green.
similar.a: get.

similar.q: Type 1: If you mix them now, you ____ green.
similar.a: will get.

why: False. It states a general scientific fact, so it is a zero conditional (If + present, present).
Type 1 uses "will" in the main clause for a specific future result.
So the statement is false.
questions.tip: Type 1 (real future): If + present, will + verb. Type 2 (unreal present/future): If + past, would + verb.

why: Answer A: deciding how many children to have and when
In population studies, "family planning" refers to controlling the number and spacing of children.
It is linked to health and economic development.
The other meanings do not fit the topic.
